correctness.rationale: Exact structural equivalence: any missing irreducible P below half degree supplies composite unit P^2; every reducible representative below modulus degree has a small irreducible factor and so cannot be a unit. Constants exclude q>2. Degree product S(3)=10 and the existence of an irreducible of every degree prove no cases above degree six. Exact polynomial totient gives the sharp order 12. A direct gcd/irreducibility enumeration for all moduli through degree eight reproduces the 18 cases and orders, independently of the universal proof.

value.rationale: The full finite-field analogue for complete prime-unit groups answers a natural concrete subcase of Li Question 6.6, classifying all coefficient fields and moduli (18 binary moduli only), with an exact obstruction criterion, degree cutoff, and sharp group-order maximum 12. This is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary bound-limited slice, though its proof is elementary. It does not claim the unresolved subgroup-order, compactness, or infinitude problems.
